newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE-EAST AFRICA FLIGHTS MOSTLY ESCAPE KENYA ACTION.
newsitem.headline: UAE-EAST AFRICA FLIGHTS MOSTLY ESCAPE KENYA ACTION.

text.p: Freight forwarders doing business from the United Arab Emirates to east Africa and many airlines operating on the route say they suffered flight delays during a Kenyan air traffic controllers go-slow.
But most say the delays had not been too severe and only a few flights had been cancelled.

A Gulf Air spokesman in Bahrain said the go-slow had caused the cancellation of two flights between Nairobi and Entebbe on Wednesday and Thursday, but flights between Nairobi and the Gulf were not affected.
"We have a flight to Nairobi today," a spokesman said.
Kenya's labour minister said at 0940 GMT on Thursday, the sixth day of the industrial action, that the go-slow had ended with agreement and flights had returned to normal.

"We are having a lot of delays, but none that we cannot live with. We have not had any cancellations and delays have at best been two hours, and at worst eight to 10 hours," said a forwarder dominant on the UAE to east Africa route.
"Our goods are mainly electronics, textiles and spare parts, so they aren't really spoilt by delays, unlike perishables," said another forwarder who handles UAE-Kenya air shipments.
Emirates airline said it was largely unaffected by the go-slow.
"In terms of cargo handling we had no problems in Nairobi. There may have been certain small delays but on the whole we were not affected," an Emirates official said.
Kenya Airways said its flight from Nairobi which arrived in Dubai on Tuesday had been delayed by some 2-1/2 hours but Thursday's flight had operated as normal.
Sharjah airport said only a few flights had been delayed.
